title: 60 SQL Practice Queries with Answers: PostgreSQL Interview Drills
summary: Sixty solved PostgreSQL queries on one employees/departments/orders schema, ordered from basic SELECTs through filtering, aggregates, joins, subqueries, window functions and CTEs to classic interview scenarios. Each task shows the solution and the result it returns on the sample data.

chapters.title: The Practice Schema and How to Use This Book
points: Table employees(id, name, email, dept_id, manager_id, salary, hire_date): one row per person, manager_id is NULL for the CEO
Table departments(id, name, location): one row per department, some departments have no employees
Table orders(id, employee_id, customer, amount, order_date, status): status is 'new', 'shipped' or 'cancelled' and may be NULL
Engine: PostgreSQL 16, every solution is plain SQL runnable in psql
Roadmap: basics, filtering, aggregates, joins, subqueries, window functions, CTEs, interview scenarios
Each page follows task, solution code, result on the sample data
Tip: try the task yourself before reading the solution
60 tasks in total, ordered from basic to advanced

chapters.title: SQL Cheatsheet: Patterns to Remember
points: Logical order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT
NULL rules: use IS NULL and IS DISTINCT FROM, never = NULL; COUNT(col) skips NULLs
WHERE filters rows, HAVING filters groups
Join picker: INNER for matches only, LEFT keeps the left side, anti-join is LEFT JOIN plus IS NULL
EXISTS and NOT EXISTS beat IN and NOT IN when NULLs are possible
ROW_NUMBER is unique, RANK leaves gaps, DENSE_RANK has none
Window frames: ORDER BY alone defaults to RANGE, so write ROWS for running totals and LAST_VALUE
Top N per group: ROW_NUMBER in a CTE, then filter rn <= N
Gaps and islands: subtract ROW_NUMBER from the date to group consecutive runs
Median and percentiles: percentile_cont ... WITHIN GROUP
